relevance_rank_note: Runs against H4: in four cell types apoE4 is retained LESS than apoE3 from apoE-enriched beta-VLDL, with 4 C binding of the two isoforms equal and beta-VLDL uptake enhanced equally, and the differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans rather than by LDLR or LRP, which decisions.md admits only as a co-receptor; no apoE-receptor affinity is measured.

description: In a CHO pulse-chase, equal amounts of apoE3- and apoE4-enriched beta-VLDL bound at 4 C, yet after warming to 37 C about 2-fold more apoE3 than apoE4 was retained in the cells at 30, 60 and 120 min, so equal binding gave unequal retention and apoE4 was retained less.
quote: As summarized in TableII, the amounts of apoE3 and apoE4 bound at 4 °C (zero time) were similar; however, the amount of apoE3 in the cells (internalized = accumulated or retained) after 30, 60, and 120 min at 37 °C was approximately 2-fold greater than the amount of apoE4.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (equal cell-surface binding but about half as much apoE retained intracellularly)
system: Wild-type CHO cells incubated 1 h at 4 C with beta-VLDL enriched with human plasma 125I-apoE3 or 125I-apoE4 at an apoE:beta-VLDL protein ratio of 1.5:1, washed, warmed to 37 C for 30, 60 and 120 min, with medium analysed for degraded and trichloroacetic acid-precipitable apoE and cells washed with 10 mM suramin before counting; one experiment in quadruplicate, repeated three times with similar results. The differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans: it is abolished by heparinase and in HSPG-deficient and proteoglycan-deficient CHO cells, and it persists in LDL receptor-negative, LRP-negative and LDLR/LRP double-negative fibroblasts, so neither LDLR nor LRP is required.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; all values are printed in Table II and its footnote. against: true because the hypothesis predicts tighter apoE4 adhesion and greater apoE4 retention, and this result is the opposite with binding equal. Effect detail: 4 C binding apoE3 399 vs apoE4 378 ng/mg cell protein; retained apoE3/apoE4 157/84 at 30 min, 123/55 at 60 min, 78/27 at 120 min ng/mg cell protein. n = quadruplicate within one experiment repeated three times; recorded as 4 because the table footnote reports one quadruplicate experiment. No P value is printed for any apoE3-versus-apoE4 contrast in this table.

description: In the same CHO pulse-chase more intact trichloroacetic acid-precipitable apoE4 than apoE3 reappeared in the medium, especially at 30 and 60 min, consistent with apoE4 being released from the cells rather than held.
quote: Of interest was the greater amount of apoE4 that appeared in the medium during the incubation period, especially at 30 and 60 min.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more intact apoE released back to the medium, less retained)
system: Wild-type CHO cells pulsed 1 h at 4 C with beta-VLDL enriched with human plasma 125I-apoE3 or 125I-apoE4, washed, warmed to 37 C for 30, 60 and 120 min, trichloroacetic acid-precipitable intact 125I-apoE measured in the medium; one experiment in quadruplicate, repeated three times with similar results. The differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans: it is abolished by heparinase and in HSPG-deficient and proteoglycan-deficient CHO cells, and it persists in LDL receptor-negative, LRP-negative and LDLR/LRP double-negative fibroblasts, so neither LDLR nor LRP is required.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Effect is qualitative because the authors state the direction without printing a ratio for released intact apoE; the table values are given in the description rather than converted. Effect detail: released intact (TCA-precipitable) apoE3/apoE4 182/245 at 30 min, 181/238 at 60 min, 232/225 ng/mg cell protein at 120 min, so the difference is present at 30 and 60 min and gone at 120 min. against: true. The authors offer two readings of the same data, preferential release of apoE4 versus sequestration of apoE3 into a compartment unavailable for release, and do not choose between them.

description: Over 2-48 h of incubation with apoE-enriched beta-VLDL, Neuro-2a cells accumulated about 1.8-fold more immunoreactive apoE3 than apoE4 at 2 h and about 1.6-fold more at 48 h, so apoE4 was retained less throughout.
quote: At the earliest time point (2 h), the cells contained approximately 1.8-fold more apoE3 than apoE4. This difference in the level of immunoreactive apoE was maintained for up to 48 h (~1.6-fold more apoE3 than apoE4) (Fig. 3).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (less intracellular apoE accumulated and retained)
system: Neuro-2a mouse neuroblastoma cells incubated 2-48 h with beta-VLDL enriched with human plasma apoE3 or apoE4, permeabilised and immunostained with a polyclonal anti-apoE antibody that detects apoE3 and apoE4 equally on Western blots, relative fluorescence intensity quantified by confocal microscopy. The differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans: it is abolished by heparinase and in HSPG-deficient and proteoglycan-deficient CHO cells, and it persists in LDL receptor-negative, LRP-negative and LDLR/LRP double-negative fibroblasts, so neither LDLR nor LRP is required.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Figure 3 has no lettered panels, so the location is recorded as the whole single-panel figure. Effect recorded as the 2 h value 1.8x; Effect detail: ~1.8-fold more apoE3 than apoE4 at 2 h, ~1.6-fold at 48 h. n = an average of 60 cells from at least six different fields per time point, per the legend; the number of independent experiments is not stated. The Results text and legend print no P value for this contrast. against: true, apoE4 accumulates and is retained less.

description: With 125I-apoE-enriched beta-VLDL, cell association of apoE3 was about 2-fold that of apoE4 in Neuro-2a cells and about 3-fold in human skin fibroblasts from 2 to 24 h, while degradation of the two isoforms did not differ significantly.
quote: In the Neuro-2a cells, the amount of apoE3 associated with the cells was twice the amount of apoE4 associated with the cells (Fig. 5 A), whereas in fibroblasts apoE3 was 3-fold more abundant than apoE4 in the cells (Fig. 5 C).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (2-3 fold less apoE associated with and retained by the cells, with degradation unchanged)
system: Neuro-2a mouse neuroblastoma cells and human skin fibroblasts incubated 2-24 h at 37 C with beta-VLDL enriched with human plasma 125I-apoE3 or 125I-apoE4, cell-associated and degraded 125I-apoE measured. The differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans: it is abolished by heparinase and in HSPG-deficient and proteoglycan-deficient CHO cells, and it persists in LDL receptor-negative, LRP-negative and LDLR/LRP double-negative fibroblasts, so neither LDLR nor LRP is required.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. Two cell types are reported in one sentence and one row is used because they are the same measurement and the same contrast; the larger fold, 3x in fibroblasts, is recorded. Effect detail: apoE3 about 2-fold apoE4 in Neuro-2a (Fig 5A) and about 3-fold in human skin fibroblasts (Fig 5C); the matching degradation panels, Fig 5B and 5D, show no significant isoform difference. If the H4 convention is one panel per row, this should be split into a Neuro-2a row and a fibroblast row. No P value or n is printed for the cell-association contrast; 'no significant difference' is stated for degradation without a number. against: true.

description: HepG2 hepatocytes incubated with 125I-apoE-enriched beta-VLDL showed about 2.5-fold greater cell association of apoE3 than apoE4 at 4 and 8 h, extending the reduced apoE4 retention to a human hepatocyte line.
quote: As shown in Table I, HepG2 cells incubated with125I-apoE3 plus β-VLDL displayed about 2.5-fold greater cell association of apoE compared with cells incubated with125I-apoE4 plus β-VLDL.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (about 2.5-fold less apoE associated with and retained by hepatocytes)
system: HepG2 human hepatoma cells incubated 4 and 8 h with beta-VLDL enriched with human plasma 125I-apoE3 or 125I-apoE4, cell-associated 125I-apoE measured in ng per mg cell protein; two independent experiments performed in duplicate. The differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans: it is abolished by heparinase and in HSPG-deficient and proteoglycan-deficient CHO cells, and it persists in LDL receptor-negative, LRP-negative and LDLR/LRP double-negative fibroblasts, so neither LDLR nor LRP is required.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; values are printed in Table I. Effect detail: apoE3 1062 +/- 171 vs apoE4 515 +/- 10 ng/mg cell protein at 4 h, and 1466 +/- 38 vs 683 +/- 6 at 8 h. n = 2 independent experiments in duplicate, recorded as the number of independent experiments. No P value is printed. against: true.

description: Cell association of 125I-beta-VLDL by Neuro-2a cells was enhanced about 1.7-fold by apoE3 and by apoE4 alike, so the two isoforms promoted binding and internalisation of the lipoprotein particle equally; a null on uptake.
quote: There was therefore no major isoform-specific difference in the ability of apoE3 or apoE4 to promote the binding and internalization of 125I-β-VLDL, suggesting that a similar amount of β-VLDL was internalized.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no change in beta-VLDL cell association, binding and internalisation)
system: Neuro-2a mouse neuroblastoma cells incubated at 37 C with 125I-beta-VLDL alone or beta-VLDL enriched with human plasma apoE3 or apoE4 at an apoE:beta-VLDL protein ratio of 1.5:1, cell association measured in ng per mg cell protein. The differential is mediated by cell surface heparan sulfate proteoglycans: it is abolished by heparinase and in HSPG-deficient and proteoglycan-deficient CHO cells, and it persists in LDL receptor-negative, LRP-negative and LDLR/LRP double-negative fibroblasts, so neither LDLR nor LRP is required.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. against: true as a null on the uptake surrogate. Effect detail: maximal beta-VLDL cell association alone about 225 ng/mg cell protein, enhanced about 1.7-fold by either isoform; the authors print the same fold for both arms and no apoE4-versus-apoE3 ratio, so eff is qualitative rather than a fold. The companion DiI panel Fig 1B shows apoE4 stimulating uptake slightly more than apoE3 with p < 0.02, which is a different measurement in a different panel and is not recorded here; a reviewer may want that as its own row, in which case it is a small finding in the pro-H4 direction on uptake.
